title: Student Grades Struct
story: Report card season! You want to calculate your average grade and figure out which subject you crushed. No more manual math — your code will analyze the scores for you.
why: Computing statistics from multiple fields teaches you to write methods that aggregate data and return meaningful summaries.
analogy: A Student struct is like a report card. Methods are like the summary section — they compute GPA, find the best subject, and assign letter grades without you doing the math.
try_it: Add a `history` subject to the Student struct. Update `average` and `highest_subject` to include it. Test with all four subjects.
tips: Use `as Float64` to convert Int to Float64 before dividing — otherwise division truncates
Methods can call other methods on the same struct — `average()` inside `letter_grade()`
When finding the max of multiple fields, compare each one against all others with `>=`
common_mistakes: Dividing Int by Int and expecting a decimal — `(math + science + english) / 3` gives integer division; use `/ 3.0` after casting
Using `>` instead of `>=` when comparing for highest — if two subjects tie, `>=` ensures one is selected
Hardcoding a return value and forgetting to return the full range — every path through `if/elif` must lead to a return
